info.name: Steakz Restaurant Portal API
info.description:
All Steakz endpoints, grouped by role.

**How to use:** choose the *Steakz — Local* or *Steakz — Production* environment, then run the whole collection with the Collection Runner (folders run in order: log in → book → order → kitchen → deliver → reports → admin → access control). Every request has tests.

Tokens are saved automatically by folder 0. Demo password: `password123` (admin: `admin123`).

item.name: 0. Log in (run first)
item.description: Logs in as every role and stores each JWT in a collection variable. All later requests use these tokens.

item.name: Login as Chef — Manchester (for branch isolation test)
1. Authentication
item.description: Register (always creates a CUSTOMER), login and current user.

item.description: Anyone can browse branches and menus.

item.name: Branch with tables + menu (free tables at a time)

exec: // A random evening slot 20–80 days ahead, so repeated runs don't clash.
const steak = b.menuItems.find(m => m.isAvailable && m.category === 'Steaks') || b.menuItems.find(m => m.isAvailable);
const side = b.menuItems.find(m => m.isAvailable && m.category === 'Sides') || steak;

item.name: 3. Customer — book a table and order
item.description: Customer books a table (status PENDING) and orders food linked to the booking.

item.name: Book the same table again → 409 (double booking)
Place an order on my booking

exec: pm.test("Order is PENDING (sent to kitchen)", () => pm.expect(o.status).to.eql("PENDING"));

item.name: 4. Chef — kitchen queue
item.description: Branch-scoped: the chef only sees and changes orders of their own branch.

exec: pm.test("The customer's order is in the queue", () => pm.expect(list.map(o => o.id)).to.include(pm.collectionVariables.get("orderId") * 1));
